1. The appellant has filed this criminal appeal under Section 29 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (hereinafter referred to the "said Act") against the ex parte judgment dated 23.05.2022 (hereinafter referred to the impugned judgment) passed by Ld. MM-01 (Mahila Court), North-West, Rohini Courts, Delhi in a complaint case bearing Ct. Case No. 19004/2016,
whereby the Ld. Trial court vide the said CA No. 116/2022 Jyoti V. Sandeep @ Monu & Anr. Page No. 1 of 13 impugned judgment, directed the respondent No.1- herein/husband to pay a sum of Rs.3,000/- pm towards the maintenance of the petitioner-therein/appellant-herein till the time she is legally entitled to be maintained by him as per law.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1/husband was also directed to provide an alternate accommodation to the petitioner/appellant according to the standard of living maintained by her in the matrimonial home or to pay rent in lieu of alternate accommodation to the petitioner/appellant, subject to placing on record rent agreement and rent receipts.
Vide the impugned judgment, the Ld. MM declined the prayers of the petitioner /appellant for protection order and custody of the minor children.

The respondent No.1/husband was also directed to pay Rs.5,000/- in total to the appellant/wife as compensation for the harassment Smt. Jyoti vs Sh. Sandeep @ Monu (Husband) on 14 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147201041/
1 suffered by her due to domestic violence as well as for loss of time and money spent in prosecuting the said application.

2. The brief facts, as set out in the present appeal, are that marriage between appellant and respondent No.1 was solemnized on 07.12.2007 as per Hindu rites and ceremonies and from the said wedlock, two children namely Himanshu and Kartik were born.
The appellant-wife filed a complaint u/s 12 of DV Act against the respondent No.1-herein and his family members.
In the said complaint case, the appellant-herein alleged that she was physically assaulted, tortured and beaten up by the respondents-therein for not fulfilling their illegal demand of dowry.

The appellant-herein/wife has also alleged that respondent-herein failed to make any provision for maintenance to her despite the fact that he has sufficient source of income of Rs.2,50,000/- pm from his businesses including illegal works CA No. 116/2022 Jyoti V. Sandeep @ Monu & Anr. Page No. 2 of 13 and rental income of Rs.20,000/- pm.
The appellant-herein sought various reliefs in her application/petition u/s 12 of the said Act.
In the said complaint case, summoning qua respondent Nos. 4 and 5 were declined vide order dt. 02.12.2016 and respondent Nos. 1 to 3 were proceeded ex parte vide order dt.12.12.2018.

After the ex parte evidence of the appellant-wife, the final arguments on behalf of the appellant- herein/complainant-therein were heard and Ld. Trial Court passed the impugned judgment dt.
23.05.2022.
3.

Aggrieved by the said impugned judgment, the appellant has preferred the present appeal on the grounds among others that the impugned judgment was passed in mechanical manner and without going into the merits of the case.

The respondent No.1 is a man of means as he owns a meat shop at Jahangir Puri, Delhi from which he is earning around Rs.1,50,000/- pm apart from rental income and income through other illegal means and in order to mislead the Ld. MM, the respondent No.1 took the defence that the said meat shop does not belong to him and same is being run by some other person.
Ld. MM has not taken into consideration the material placed i.e. photographs etc. and passed the impugned judgment.

As per the circular of State Government in the year 2022 regarding minimum wages, the minimum wages of semi-skilled labours have been increased from Rs.17,693/-
to Rs.18,187/- pm and for skilled workers, the wages has been increased from Rs.17,743/- to Rs.20,019/- pm.
The maintenance of Rs.3000/- pm is very meager amount considering the status and income of the respondent No.1.

The respondent No.1 deliberately and intentionally with sole intention to harass and humiliate the CA No. 116/2022 Jyoti V. Sandeep @ Monu & Anr. Page No. 3 of 13 appellant, wants the appellant to live in a Jhuggi in a slum area as he has refused to arrange a suitable rented accommodation for the appellant.

The respondent-herein is not allowing the appellant to enter into her matrimonial home and the appellant is being forced to live at a rental accommodation which is not habitable in any manner and moreover such place is not right for the safety and security of the appellant.
The respondent may be directed to permit the appellant to enter into the matrimonial home.
The real and actual income of the respondent No.1 is more than Rs.2,50,000/- pm.

The appellant has prayed to set aside the impugned judgment dt. 23.05.2022.
4.
The respondents-herein have filed reply to the appeal and raised the preliminary objections that the Ld. MM has rightly passed the impugned judgment dt. 23.05.2022 after hearing the parties.

It was the appellant who time and again used to leave the matrimonial home and that too without informing the respondent No.1 and other family members.

I have heard the Ld. Counsel for the parties and I have also gone through the written arguments filed on behalf of parties and also the impugned judgment dt.23.05.2022 as well as materials available on record.

6. Ld. Counsel for the appellant argued that the marriage of the appellant was solemnized on false pretext by saying that the respondent No.1 is a government servant but he is involved in illegal activities.
She was subjected to cruelties and beatings.
The respondent No.1 runs a meat shop.
The respondent No.1 is earning Rs.1,50,000/- pm apart from rental income.
His total monthly income is Rs.2,50,000/- and he is living luxurious life.
The photographs of the meat shop placed on record were not considered by the Ld. MM.
Even the minimum wages for semi-skilled labours in Delhi has been increased from Rs.17,693/- to Rs.18,187/- pm but a meager amount of Rs.3,000/- pm was awarded as maintenance.
The respondent No.1 is involved in several criminal activities.
The respondent No.1 has not arranged a rented accommodation for the appellant in compliance of the judgment dt. 23.05.2022 and threatened her that she will be forced to live in a Jhuggi.

As per the judgment in the case of Satish Chandra Ahuja Vs. Sneha Ahuja in Civil Appeal No. 2483/2020 (arising out of SLP No. 1048 of 2020), an aggrieved person must be given rental accommodation at her matrimonial home by the husband when the rental accommodation for the appellant is not safe for her life and safety.

The appellant/wife is a house-wife and has no source of income.
7.

Ld. Counsel for the respondents argued that the appellant never performed her part of obligations towards the CA No. 116/2022 Jyoti V. Sandeep @ Monu & Anr. Page No. 5 of 13 respondent No.1 as well as her children.
It is the appellant who on her own left the matrimonial home without informing the respondents on 24.12.2015.
The children were aged about 3 and 7 years respectively when the appellant/wife left her matrimonial home.
The children are studying in 7 th and 4th standard.
The respondent No.1 is taking care of the children who are living with him.
The appellant has not filed any case for custody right of the children.
There is no rental income of the respondent No.1.
He is a helping labour and earning Rs.15,000/- pm and from this meager amount he has also to maintain his both children and family members.
No meat shop is being run by the respondent No.1.
No proof is filed which shows that he is running a meat shop.
The allegations regarding illegal activities and huge earning against the respondent No.1 are false and frivolous.
Therefore, this appeal is liable to be dismissed.

sentences.text: Perusal of record reveals that there is no dispute about the marriage and relationship of husband and wife and the children.
The appellant-herein/wife has made allegations of domestic violence against the respondents-herein and his family members in her complaint/petition filed before the Ld. Trial Court.
After filing of DIR, the respondent Nos. 1 to 3-therein were summoned.
Summoning qua respondent Nos. 4 & 5- therein were declined vide order dt. 02.12.2016.
Thereafter, the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 have not filed written statement/reply.
They also did not appear in the proceedings before the Ld. MM and they were proceeded ex parte on 12.12.2018.
The appellant- herein/wife examined herself as CW1 on 22.12.2021 before the Ld. Trial Court and tendered her evidence by way of affidavit CA No. 116/2022 Jyoti V. Sandeep @ Monu & Anr.

Page No. 6 of 13 Ex.CW1/A and relied upon the documents from Ex.CW1/1 to Ex.CW1/11 and also document Mark-A.

As per the detailed income affidavit filed by the appellant-herein / wife before the Ld. Trial Court,
she is 8 th passed and she has no source of income.
In her income affidavit, she has stated that she is staying with her parents who are government servants.
She has three dependents but has not mentioned the details of dependents.
In the relevant information relating to the spouse, the appellant/wife has stated that the respondent/husband is 10 th passed.
She also stated that respondent/husband is running / indulged in various business of selling liquor illegally and illegal work and earning Rs.30,000/- pm.

Furthermore, he is running meat shops at C-Block, Jahangir Puri and village Kheri, Delhi from which he is earning more than Rs.1,50,000/- and also business of selling the animals etc. from which he is earning Rs.10,000/- pm and also having rental income of Rs.20,000/- of six rooms thus, in total the respondent/husband is earning more than Rs.2,50,000/-
pm.
The appellant/wife also stated that the respondent/husband is having Alto car, scooty bearing last digits no. 6919 colour white and properties in his name.
In her income affidavit, the appellant/wife also stated that her two children namely Himanshu aged 7 years and Kartik 3 years are in the custody of the respondent/husband.
She has mentioned her total monthly expenditure as Rs.30,000/- approximately.
As per her income affidavit, she has no liability.
She is living in 50 square yards residential accommodation with her father who is the owner of the said residential accommodation.
She has mentioned her CA No. 116/2022 Jyoti V. Sandeep @ Monu & Anr. Page No. 7 of 13 status as 'lower'.
The respondent No.1/ husband has not filed detailed income affidavit before the Ld. Trial Court.

10. I would place a reliance upon the judgment reported in the case of Bhuwan Mohan Singh Vs.
Meena & Ors.
2014AIR (SC) 2875, wherein it was held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court on the concept of sustenance and obligation of husband that the concept of sustenance does not necessarily mean to lead the life of an animal, feel like an unperson to be thrown away from grace and roam for her basic maintenance somewhere else.

T h e petitioner-therein/appellant-herein alleged that the respondent No.1-herein/husband is earning a total income of Rs.2,50,000/- pm from his business of meat shop, rental income and other illegal business.

Whereas, the respondent No.1/husband alleged that the appellant/wife has left the matrimonial house on her own without any reason leaving behind the two minor children with the respondent No.1/husband.
The appellant/wife has filed copy of RC of scooty in the name of respondent No.1/husband but the RC of the car is in the name of Shakuntala and not in the name of respondent No.1/husband.

The appellant/wife in support of her claim that the respondent No.1/husband is running a meat shop and having a rental income from his property, filed photographs Ex.CW1/9 (colly.) and Ex.CW1/10(colly.).

These photographs do not show that the respondent No.1/husband is the owner of the said meat shop or the said meat shop is being run by him or that he is getting rental income from the said property being the owner of the said property.
The appellant/wife has also not filed any affidavit u/s 65B of Indian Evidence Act.
On the basis of these photographs quantum of income of the respondent No.1- herein/husband cannot be decided.

However, these photographs including the photographs of Car and its registration status Ex.CW1/6 (colly.) which is in the name of respondent No.2- herein i.e. the mother of the respondent No.1-herein/husband and photographs Ex.CW1/11 (colly) show that the respondent No.1/husband is living a good standard but exact income of the respondent No.1/husband cannot be decided on the basis of such photographs. The respondent No.1-herein/husband has neither filed his reply/WS to the complaint u/s 12 of the said Act nor his CA No. 116/2022 Jyoti V. Sandeep @ Monu & Anr.
Page No. 9 of 13 detailed income affidavit before the Ld. MM.
As per detailed income affidavit of the appellant/wife, the respondent No.1/husband is 10 th passed.
In the absence of exact income of the respondent/husband, the Ld. MM assessed the income of the respondent No.1/husband on the basis of minimum wages applicable in Delhi.

12. In the case of Sh. Bharat Hegde V. Smt. Saroj Hegde, 140 (2007) DLT 161, the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in para No. 6 held that " While considering a claim for interim maintenance, the court has to keep in mind the status of the parties, reasonable wants of the applicant, the income and property of the applicant.

entities.text: Bharat Hegde V. Smt. Saroj Hegde, 140 (2007) DLT 161
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Conversely, requirements of the non applicant, the income and property of the non applicant and additionally the other family members to be maintained by the non applicant
have to be taken into all.

Whilst it is important to insure that the maintenance awarded to the applicant is sufficient to enable the applicant to live in somewhat the same degree of comfort as in the matrimonial home, but it should not be so exorbitant that the non applicant is unable to pay.

The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in para No. 19 of the judgment in the case of Bharat Hegde (supra)
further held that "As noted herein above, unfortunately, nobody pays proper taxes to the Government.
Self employed persons seldom disclose their true income.

Prudence and worldly wisdom gained by a judge before whom citizens of all stratas of society litigate it can always be used Smt. Jyoti vs Sh. Sandeep @ Monu (Husband) on 14 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147201041/
5 by a Judge to broadly ascertain as to what is going on in the society.
By no means, said knowledge can be used where law requires a fact to be conclusively proved.

But where the law requires a Judge to form an opinion based on a host of primary data, a Judge can formulate an opinion pertaining to the likely income from the capital assets of the husband".
13.

In the case of Sujit Kumar V. Vandana in MAT.
APP. (F.C.) 35/2015, the Hon'ble Delhi High Court held that "Where the parties do not come forward with exact income they have, the Court would have no alternative but to apply its guess work.
In the decision CA No. 116/2022 Jyoti V. Sandeep @ Monu & Anr.

Page No. 10 of 13 reported as 140 (2007) DLT 161 Sh. Bharat Hegde Vs. Smt. Saroj Hegde, it was held that under noted eleven factors have to be taken into account:-
1. Status of the parties.
2. Reasonable wants of the claimant.
3. The independent income and property of the claimant.
4. The number of persons, the non applicant has to maintain.
5. The amount should aid the applicant to live in a similar life style as he/she enjoyed in the matrimonial home.
6. Non-applicant's liabilities, if any.
7. Provisions for food, clothing, shelter, education, medical attendance and treatment etc. of the applicant.
8. Payment capacity of the non applicant.
9. Some guess work is not ruled out while estimating the income of the non applicant when all the sources or correct sources are not disclosed.
10. The non applicant to defray the cost of litigation.
11. The amount awarded Under Section 125 Cr.PC is adjustable against the amount awarded Under Section 24 of the Act".
14.

In view of the facts and circumstances of the case, income affidavit of the appellant/wife,
documents and the above judgments, I am of the considered opinion that there is no sufficient documents on record which show that the respondent No.1/husband is earning the alleged handsome income of Rs.2,50,000/- per month.

The respondent No.1-herein/husband neither filed written statement/reply nor the detailed income affidavit and was proceeded ex parte before the Ld.

sentences.text: The detailed income affidavit of the appellant/wife and also the documents filed on record have also been perused and considered by this court in this appeal.
The photographs including the photographs of Car and its registration status Ex.CW1/6 (colly.) which is in the name of respondent No.2- CA No. 116/2022 Jyoti V. Sandeep @ Monu & Anr.

Page No. 11 of 13 herein i.e. the mother of the respondent No.1-herein/husband and the photographs Ex.CW1/11 (colly) show that the respondent No.1-herein/husband withheld information of his income and that he is living a good standard.

It is a well recognized principle of law that where a person withholds vital information, a presumption arises against him that had he disclosed the information, the same would have been adverse to him.
It is admitted by the parties that both the children are living with the respondent No.1/husband.

The respondent/ husband is duty bound and cannot escape from his liability to maintain his wife for her day to day expenses as well as medical expenses as per his status and income, if the appellant / wife is neither working nor earning any amount.
Some guess work is not ruled out while estimating the income of the respondent No.1/husband when all the sources or correct sources are not disclosed.

15. As per the Order dt.23.05.2022 issued from Government of NCT of Delhi (Labour Department),
the minimum wages for the unskilled person was Rs.16,506/- pm as on 01.04.2022 and for matriculate person but not graduate the minimum wages was Rs.20,019/- as on 01.04.2022.

Considering the above discussions, day to day expenses in Delhi and status of the parties and also to meet the ends of justice, the impugned judgment dt. 23.05.2022 is modified to the extent that the respondent No.1-herein/husband shall pay the amount of Rs.4,500/- pm instead of Rs.3000/- pm to the appellant- herein/wife as maintenance from the date of filing of the said petition till the time she is legally entitled to be maintained by him as per law.

As far as residence order is concerned, the appellant/wife has proved that she has been a victim of domestic CA No. 116/2022 Jyoti V. Sandeep @ Monu & Anr. Page No. 12 of 13 violence committed by the respondent No.1/husband.

The appellant/wife has also been living separately since 24.12.2015 and if she is allowed to live with the respondent No.1-herein/ husband, it will not safe for the appellant/wife and in the best interest of appellant/wife, the Ld. MM has rightly passed the impugned judgment directing the respondent No.1- herein/husband to provide an alternate accommodation according to the standard of living maintained by her in the matrimonial home or to pay rent in lieu of alternate accommodation to the appellant/wife, subject to placing on record rent agreement and rent receipts.
Maintenance amount awarded in any other proceedings shall be adjusted in this case.
The rest of the directions in the impugned judgment dt.23.05.2022 shall remain the same.
Accordingly, this appeal is partly allowed.
Trial Court record along with copy of this Judgment be sent back to the Ld. Trial Court.
Appeal file be consigned to Record Room.

The respondent/ husband is duty bound and cannot escape from his liability to maintain his wife for her day to day expenses as well as medical expenses as per his status and income, if the appellant / wife is neither working nor earning any amount.
Some guess work is not ruled out while estimating the income of the respondent No.1/husband when all the sources or correct sources are not disclosed.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Considering the above discussions, day to day expenses in Delhi and status of the parties and also to meet the ends of justice, the impugned judgment dt. 23.05.2022 is modified to the extent that the respondent No.1-herein/husband shall pay the amount of Rs.4,500/- pm instead of Rs.3000/- pm to the appellant- herein/wife as maintenance from the date of filing of the said petition till the time she is legally entitled to be maintained by him as per law.
As far as residence order is concerned, the appellant/wife has proved that she has been a victim of domestic CA No. 116/2022 Jyoti V. Sandeep @ Monu & Anr. Page No. 12 of 13 violence committed by the respondent No.1/husband.
The appellant/wife has also been living separately since 24.12.2015 and if she is allowed to live with the respondent No.1-herein/ husband, it will not safe for the appellant/wife and in the best interest of appellant/wife, the Ld. MM has rightly passed the impugned judgment directing the respondent No.1- herein/husband to provide an alternate accommodation according to the standard of living maintained by her in the matrimonial home or to pay rent in lieu of alternate accommodation to the appellant/wife, subject to placing on record rent agreement and rent receipts.
Maintenance amount awarded in any other proceedings shall be adjusted in this case.
The rest of the directions in the impugned judgment dt.23.05.2022 shall remain the same.
Accordingly, this appeal is partly allowed.
Trial Court record along with copy of this Judgment be sent back to the Ld. Trial Court.
Appeal file be consigned to Record Room.
